PortaPill, an automated pill dispenser

Capstone II / January to August 2026 / with Blaise Swan
View source on GitHub ↗

A three-compartment automated pill dispenser built around a specific reliability question. How do you actually confirm a dose was delivered, and not just commanded?

Control is split across two microcontrollers. An RP2350 (Raspberry Pi Pico 2) runs real-time motor control, scheduling, and delivery sensing. An ESP32-S3 handles the touchscreen UI, Wi-Fi, and a web dashboard hosted directly on the device so caretakers can check status from a phone browser without any cloud service in the loop.

Every dispense is verified two independent ways. An IR beam-break sensor catches pill transit through the chute, a piezoelectric sensor picks up impact in the collection drawer, and a Hall-effect sensor confirms the drawer was opened for pickup. If verification fails, the system retries automatically before reporting a persistent fault.

2 MCUs, UART-linked
